Then $$\begin{aligned} R_j&=\frac{w}{e!}j^e+O(j^{e-1}),\label{nv:GRR-rank}\\ B_0:=G+\lim_j\frac{c_1(\mathcal F_j)}{jR_j} &=\frac{f_*\beta^{e+1}}{(e+1)w}\ge0,\label{nv:GRR-base}\\ \int_U\beta^{b_0+e} &\le (e+1)^{b_0}w\,\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(B_0).\label{nv:mixed-bound} \end{aligned}$$ The limit in Equation <a href="#nv:GRR-base" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="nv:GRR-base">[nv:GRR-base]</a> is a limit of real Bott–Chern classes.
  - Explanation: Direct-image determinants give a pseudo-effective base class; flattening and mixed nef inequalities bound the total Kähler volume by its base volume.
- **claim-projective-bundle-slope-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-nv-slope-descent)): Let $Y$ be a smooth compact Kähler manifold and $\mathcal{E}$ a holomorphic vector bundle of rank at least two. Write $\pi_{\mathcal{E}}:\mathbb P_Y(\mathcal{E})\to Y$ and $\zeta_{\mathcal{E}}=c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(\mathcal{E})}(1))$. Suppose that a real class $D$ on $Y$ satisfies $$c_1(\mathcal{H})\le kD \quad\text{whenever}\quad 0\ne\bigl(\mathcal{H}\longrightarrow\mathcal{E}^{\otimes k}\bigr)$$ for a line bundle $\mathcal{H}$ and integer $k\ge0$. For a real class $A$ on $Y$ and a real number $b\ge0$, $$\label{nv:slope-descent-equation} \pi_{\mathcal{E}}^*A+b\zeta_{\mathcal{E}}\ge0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A+bD\ge0 .$$
  - Explanation: A tensor-line slope bound and direct-image determinants descend pseudo-effectivity from a projective bundle to the base.
- **claim-selected-diagonal-mass** (bound, [source](#stmt-nv-diagonal-mass)): There are constants $c_n,C_n>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $q$, one can choose a rational number $$c_nA_q\le s\le C_nA_q$$ and a Kähler current $T$ in $C_s$ with analytic singularities, not generically singular on $E$, with the following property. On a smooth projective modification $h:U\to E$, its restricted mass has a rational-divisor approximation $$\label{nv:selected-decomposition} h^*(2M+s\zeta)=\beta+\{D'\}, \qquad \beta\ \text{Kähler},\quad D'\ge0\ \text{rational},$$ which retains all log-ideal orders of $T\|_E$. If $f:U\to Z$ is the natural map and $$w=\int_{U_z}\beta^{d-1}$$ on a general fiber, then $$\label{nv:selected-w} w\ge c_ns^{d-1}.$$
  - Explanation: Integration of diagonal restricted volumes selects a rational parameter and a current whose fibre volume retains a positive rank fraction.
- **claim-incidence-pole-transfer** (bound, [source](#stmt-nv-incidence-pole)): The pole just defined satisfies $$\label{nv:pole-transfer} b_V\ge s-C_n .$$
  - Explanation: Conormal slope descent and the original point bound force almost the full diagonal parameter into the incidence pole.
- **claim-determinant-common-order** (bound, [source](#stmt-nv-determinant-order)): On a smooth projective modification $h_+:U^+\to E^+$ one can choose an approximation $$\label{nv:plus-decomposition} h_+^*(2p_+^*M+s\zeta)=\beta^++\{D^+\}, \qquad \beta^+\ \text{Kähler},\quad D^+\ge0\ \text{rational},$$ retaining the log-ideal orders of $T\|_E$, such that the general fiber volume $w^+$ of $\beta^+$ over $Z^+$ satisfies $w^+\ge w/2$. Let $f_+:U^+\to Z^+$ be the natural map and put $$\Lambda^+=s h_+^*\mathcal O_{E^+}(1)-\mathcal O_{U^+}(D^+),\qquad \mathcal F_j^+=(f_+)_*\mathcal O_{U^+}(j\Lambda^+),\qquad R_j^+=\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}\mathcal F_j^+ .$$ For every sufficiently large divisible $j$, write $$\iota_j:\mathcal F_j^+\hookrightarrow p_+^*\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\Omega_Z,\qquad \varphi_j:\det\mathcal F_j^+\longrightarrow \bigwedge^{R_j^+}\!\bigl(p_+^*\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\Omega_Z\bigr)$$ for the inclusion and its nonzero determinant map. Here $\det\mathcal F_j^+=(\bigwedge^{R_j^+}\mathcal F_j^+)^{**}$, and the determinant map extends across the complement of the locally free locus, which has codimension at least two. Localize a coordinate local ring of $Z^+$ at the height-one prime of $J_+$, obtaining a discrete valuation ring $R$ with uniformizer $u$. In local frames over $R$, define $$h_j=\min\{\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_u(c):c\text{ is a nonzero coefficient of }\varphi_j\}.$$ Equivalently, $h_j$ is the minimum order of the maximal minors of $\iota_j$; it is independent of the frames. If $\sigma_{J_+}$ is the canonical section of $\mathcal O_{Z^+}(J_+)$, then $\varphi_j$ factors as $$\det\mathcal F_j^+ \xrightarrow{\ \cdot\sigma_{J_+}^{h_j}\ } \det\mathcal F_j^+(h_jJ_+) \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde\varphi_j\ } \bigwedge^{R_j^+}\!\bigl(p_+^*\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\Omega_Z\bigr),$$ where $\widetilde\varphi_j$ is holomorphic. The common order satisfies $$\label{nv:determinant-order-equation} h_j\ge c_n\,jR_j^+s ,$$ provided $q$ is sufficiently large.
  - Explanation: Incidence ideal orders force many symmetric-power coefficient rows to vanish, yielding a common positive determinant order along the exceptional base divisor.
- **claim-signed-rigidity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-signed-torsion)): Let $(X,D)$ be a dlt pair on a normal irreducible compact Kähler space, and suppose that the pair has the resolution property of Definition <a href="#def:lc-strata-resolution" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:lc-strata-resolution">16</a>. Suppose also that $X$ is globally $\mathbb Q$-factorial, that $a(X)=0$, that $X$ is simple, and that $D=\sum_{i=1}^sD_i$ is reduced. Put $L=K_X+D$, and assume the following.* 1. *The rational line $L$ is analytically nef and has an actual rational linear equivalence $$L\sim_{\mathbb Q}G=\sum_{i=1}^s a_iD_i,\qquad a_i\in\mathbb Q.$$* 2. *For some real $c>0$, the pullback of the class $\{L-cD\}$ to a projective resolution with smooth compact Kähler source is pseudo-effective.* 3. *The rational holomorphic line $L\|_D$ is semiample on the whole reduced analytic space $D$: some Cartier multiple is generated at every point of $D$.* *Then $L$ is torsion. More precisely, for some positive integer $q$, the holomorphic line $\mathcal O_X(qL)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$.
  - Explanation: A signed nef adjoint supported on a reduced boundary becomes torsion when its canonical subtraction is pseudo-effective and its whole boundary restriction is semiample on a simple space.
- **claim-signed-boundary-dimensions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-signed-boundary-geometry)): If $v=0$, then $D=0$ and $L\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$. If $v=n>0$, then $a(X)=n$. If $0<v<n$ and $r=v-1$, then $$\dim\phi(D_i)\leq r\quad\text{for every }i, \qquad \max_{a_i>0}\dim\phi(D_i)=r,$$ and $$\label{signed:small-intersections} \dim\phi\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_+\cap(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_-\cup D_0)\bigr)<r.$$ For $r=0$, the intersection in Equation <a href="#signed:small-intersections" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="signed:small-intersections">[signed:small-intersections]</a> is empty.
  - Explanation: Numerical dimension detects positive boundary components and separates their general fibres from the nonpositive signed support.
- **claim-analytic-signed-root-charts** (construction, [source](#stmt-signed-root-charts)): For each $t\in P$, after shrinking an open neighborhood $U\subset P$, choose a line $R_U$ together with an isomorphism $R_U^\ell\simeq\mathcal O_P(1)\|_U$. A comparison of two such roots on an overlap is power-compatible if its $\ell$-th power commutes with these isomorphisms. If $t\notin\phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_+)$, one may take $U$ disjoint from this closed image and set $Z_U=S=T=\varnothing$; the assertions below are then vacuous for the unique maps from the empty spaces. If $t\in\phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_+)$, there are a Hausdorff normal analytic space $Z_U$ of pure dimension $n$, considered near a reduced Cartier divisor $S$ of pure dimension $n-1$, a reduced Weil divisor $T$ with no component in common with $S$, and maps $$\pi:Z_U\longrightarrow X,\qquad g:S\longrightarrow U$$ with the following properties.* 1. *The map $g$ is proper, and $\pi\|_S$ is finite over $D_U=\phi^{-1}(U)$, with $g=\phi\pi\|_S$. Its image covers the positive components over $U$, and $$\mathcal O_S(S)\simeq g^*R_U.$$ The image of $S\cap T$ lies in $\phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_+\cap(\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}G_-\cup D_0))$. Near $S$, the underlying sets satisfy $$\pi^{-1}(\|D\|)=\|S\|\cup\|T\|.$$* 2. *The pair $(Z_U,S+T)$ is log canonical, and there is a fixed actual isomorphism of divisorial sheaves $$\label{signed:adjoint-chart} \tau:\mathcal O_{Z_U}(aS)\xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\omega_{Z_U}(S+T).$$ The spaces $Z_U$ and $S$ are Cohen–Macaulay. The support of $T$ is locally set-theoretically principal. Off $T$, the space $Z_U$ is klt and its canonical sheaf is invertible. The map $\pi$ is quasi-finite near $S\setminus T$.* 3. *Projective log resolutions of the total divisor data can be chosen with Kähler forms on neighborhoods of the compact sets over each compact fiber of $g$. Power-compatible changes of the boundary root extend to isomorphisms of ambient germs that preserve the full ideal $\mathcal O_{Z_U}(-S)$, the reduced divisor $T$, and Equation <a href="#signed:adjoint-chart" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="signed:adjoint-chart">[signed:adjoint-chart]</a>. Resolutions may be chosen functorially for these germ isomorphisms.* *Here the nonempty space $Z_U$ is a neighborhood of the whole compact fiber under consideration; no extension of $g$ to $Z_U$ is asserted.
  - Explanation: Root extraction, adjoint torsion trivialization and divisor separation produce ordinary analytic neighbourhoods with a controlled normal root line and residual poles.
- **claim-residual-pole-residue** (theorem, [source](#stmt-signed-residue)): For every $i\geq0$, the fixed adjoint isomorphism gives a split injection $$\label{signed:residue-injection} R^ig_*\mathcal O_S(aS)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow R^ih_*\omega_H(A).$$ The injection and its retraction commute with the root germ comparisons. Under a product with a manifold they are the relative canonical constructions; for absolute canonical sheaves they are tensored with the canonical line of that additional factor.
  - Explanation: The fixed adjoint isomorphism inserts the boundary line as a split summand of resolved residues with residual poles.
- **claim-localized-hodge-strictness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-signed-localized-hodge)): Let $q:\mathcal{V}\to Y$ be a holomorphic map of complex manifolds, submersive near a reduced closed analytic subspace $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V}$ of pure dimension $d$ and codimension $c_0>0$. Suppose $h=q\|_H$ is proper. Assume that locally $H$ is an SNC divisor in a smooth submanifold of codimension $c_0-1$, and that a reduced divisor $A$ is simultaneously SNC and transverse to those support equations. Assume that the components $H_i$ and $A_j$ near $H$ have finite global smooth indexing, and that every closed stratum $H_I\cap A_J$, with $I\ne\varnothing$, is smooth and proper over $Y$ and carries a global relative Kähler form. Empty or disconnected strata are allowed. Here $H_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i$ and $A_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}A_j$, with $A_\varnothing=\mathcal{V}$.* *Use right $\mathcal{D}$-modules and finite-pole local cohomology, and put $$\mathcal K_A=\mathcal H^{c_0}_{[H]}(\omega_{\mathcal{V}})(*A).$$ Its order filtration is generated from $F_0\mathcal K_A=i_*\omega_H(A)$, with $F_p=0$ for $p<0$. For $M^j=\mathcal H^j q_+\mathcal K_A$, the filtered direct image is strict at every level, and $M^j$ has a finite filtration by submodules, strict for $F$, whose quotients are polarizable real pure Hodge modules. In particular, $$\label{signed:lowest-step} F_0M^j=R^jh_*\omega_H(A)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow M^j, \qquad F_pM^j=0\quad(p<0).$$ Define the symbol morphism $$\sigma:F_0M^j\otimes T_Y\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}^F_1M^j, \qquad \sigma(m\otimes\xi)=[m\xi].$$ If $Y$ is smooth projective, then for every ample line $N$ on $Y$, $$\label{signed:symbol-vanishing} \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal O_Y}(N,\mathop{\mathrm{ker}}\sigma)=0.$$ This includes any coherent torsion in the kernel.
  - Explanation: A strict filtered direct image of finite-pole local cohomology identifies its lowest step and gives ample-to-symbol-kernel vanishing on a projective base, including torsion.
- **claim-all-finite-lifting-orders** (theorem, [source](#stmt-signed-all-orders)): For every root chart, every $j\in\mathbb Z$, and every $k\geq1$, the map of sheaves of complex vector spaces on $U$ $$\label{signed:all-order-surjection} g_*\mathcal T_{j,k+1}\longrightarrow g_*\mathcal T_{j,k}$$ is surjective. The assertion holds on every parameter germ, including germs supported at special parameters.
  - Explanation: The obstruction derivations vanish on every parameter germ, including special-parameter torsion, so every finite boundary lifting order is surjective.
- **claim-escaping-compact-fibres** (construction, [source](#stmt-signed-escaping-fibers)): Assume $0<v<n$, set $d=n-v$, and choose a positive component $D_i$ with $\dim\phi(D_i)=r$. There is a nonempty open subset $D_i^\circ\subset D_i$ with the following property. For every $x\in D_i^\circ$, there are a disk $\Delta$ about $0$, a proper flat analytic family $\mathcal{F}\to\Delta$ of compact subspaces of pure dimension $d$, and a finite morphism $$\mathcal{F}\longrightarrow X\times\Delta$$ over $\Delta$, such that every nonzero fiber has image disjoint from $D$, while $x$ is a limit of points in those images as the parameter tends to zero. Its schematic image is flat over the disk with pure $d$-dimensional fibers, whose fundamental cycles form a bounded family in the cycle space of $X$ after shrinking the disk.
  - Explanation: Formal lifting, a convergent deformation arc and finite schematic images yield bounded compact families escaping the boundary while approaching its chosen positive component.

        "exact_quote": "Let $\\nu:Z\\to X$ be a finite surjective morphism of normal irreducible complex spaces, of degree $d>0$, and let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $X$.         "anchor": "stmt-prog-mori",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(T,B+\\boldsymbol\\beta)$ be an effective compact Kähler gklt pair of dimension $d$, with $T$ globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial. Suppose that its nef b-data are globally nef on a fixed smooth carrier and that $\\{B\\}+\\beta_T$ is globally modified big. Write $\\alpha=\\{K_T+B\\}+\\beta_T$.*\n\n1.  *If $\\alpha$ is nef, there is a proper morphism with connected fibers $g:T\\to Z$ to a normal compact Kähler space and a Kähler class $\\omega_Z$ such that $\\alpha=g^*\\omega_Z$.*\n\n2.  *For a proper morphism $\\pi:T\\to V$ to a normal compact Kähler space, if $\\alpha$ is pseudo-effective over $V$, there is a chosen good log terminal model over $V$. It is nonextracting, compact Kähler and globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial. Its adjoint is nef over $V$, and on a common projective resolution its comparison with $\\alpha$ is effective and exceptional over the new model, with strictly positive coefficient at every prime contracted from $T$. The construction retains compatible forward Bott–Chern traces of the specified data on a common smooth carrier.*\n\n3.  *A compact polytope of these data on one fixed carrier has finitely many marked relative canonical models and relative weak log canonical models with normal compact Kähler targets.*\n\n*The relative assertion applies to proper morphisms, without assuming that $\\pi$ is projective. It is an assertion about a chosen model, not termination of every generalized flip sequence.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prog-integral-descent",
        "exact_quote": "Let $f:T\\to Z$ be a projective bimeromorphic contraction with normal target. Suppose an ordinary rational klt adjoint is $f$-antiample. If a Cartier line $L$ has degree zero on every contracted curve, then $f_*L$ is an invertible sheaf and evaluation is an isomorphism $$f^*(f_*L)\\simeq L.$$ The same conclusion holds for an ordinary dlt adjoint whose floor is rational Cartier and which is $f$-antiample. In a flip, a line with zero contracted degree therefore has the same Cartier exponent on both sides, and the two lines are pullbacks of a line on the common base.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prog-relative-klt",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\pi:T\\to V$ be projective bimeromorphic, where $V$ is a normal compact Kähler space and $T$ is normal, compact Kähler, and globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial. Let $(T,B)$ be an effective rational klt pair with rational-line adjoint $J=K_T+B$. There is a finite sequence of ordinary $J$-negative steps over $V$, all projective over $V$, whose last adjoint is curve-nef over $V$, meaning that it has nonnegative degree on every curve contracted over $V$. Every working space is compact Kähler and globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial.         "anchor": "stmt-prog-nef-trivial",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(T,B)$ be an effective rational dlt pair on a globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial compact Kähler $d$-fold, and put $J=K_T+B$.*\n\n1.  *For a sufficiently large Kähler class $\\omega$, there is an ordinary $J$-program with scaling of $\\omega$, starting with $\\{J\\}+\\omega$ Kähler. Every positive truncation is finite. If $J$ is pseudo-effective, the program either reaches a nef adjoint or has positive thresholds tending to zero. If $J$ is not pseudo-effective, the program is finite and ends with a Mori fiber contraction.*\n\n2.  *Let $P$ be a nef rational line with $mP$ Cartier, and choose $b\\in\\mathbb Q$ with $b>4dm$. The same alternatives hold for $H=J+bP$, according to pseudo-effectivity of $H$, with $\\omega$ enlarged if necessary. Every birational step is an ordinary $J$-negative step on which $P$ is trivial, and the final Mori ray, if present, is also $P$-trivial. The same line $mP$ descends through every birational contraction and pulls back to its positive side. Its traces remain analytically nef; if $P$ is semiample, its same generated multiple and associated morphism are preserved, also through the final Mori contraction.",
        "source_id": "PM-034.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Let $(T,B)$ be an effective rational dlt pair on a globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial compact Kähler space, and put $J=K_T+B$.         "exact_quote": "Let $(T,B+\\mathbf M)$ be a gklt pair on a normal compact Kähler space which is globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial, and let $A\\in H^{1,1}_{\\mathrm{BC}}(T,\\mathbb R)$ be its adjoint class. Let $f:T\\to Z$ be a projective small contraction onto a normal compact Kähler space. Suppose that the classes of all $f$-vertical curves lie on one ray $R\\subset\\overline{\\mathrm{NA}}(T)$, that $A\\cdot R<0$, and that a global line bundle $L$ satisfies $L\\cdot R<0$.*\n\n*Then $\\bigoplus_{m\\geq0}f_*L^m$ is locally finitely generated. The relative Proj of a sufficiently divisible Veronese is a projective small contraction $f^+:T^+\\to Z$, where $T^+$ is compact Kähler and globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial. The reflexive transform $L^+$ is a rational line bundle, with a positive power equal to the relatively ample tautological bundle. The transformed boundary and the same b-nef datum define a gklt pair on $T^+$, with relatively Kähler adjoint $A^+$. This is the generalized flip, with the usual strict discrepancy increase at centres in either exceptional locus.*\n\n*Moreover, if $t=(A\\cdot C)/(L\\cdot C)>0$ for an $f$-vertical curve $C$, then there is a unique $\\eta\\in H^{1,1}_{\\mathrm{BC}}(Z,\\mathbb R)$ such that $$A=t\\,c_1(L)+f^*\\eta,\\qquad\n A^+=t\\,c_1(L^+)+(f^+)^*\\eta.$$ Every class on $T$ has the corresponding forward transport with an actual exceptional-divisor correction.         "exact_quote": "Let $f:X\\to S$ be an already projective surjective morphism of normal compact Kähler spaces, with $X$ smooth. Then there is a finite chosen $A$-negative projective program over $S$, with globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial compact Kähler working spaces, and a nonextracting endpoint $X_m$ such that $$J_m\\sim_{\\mathbb R}g^*H,\n \\qquad\n A_m=g^*\\bigl(c_1(H)+\\rho^*\\beta\\bigr).$$ Here $J_m$ is the actual real-line transform of $J$, $g:X_m\\to Z$ is a projective connected-fibre morphism, $\\rho:Z\\to S$ is projective, and $H$ is an actual real line bundle ample over $S$. Thus the class on $Z$ in this formula is relatively Kähler over $S$. The generalized pair on $X_m$ is gklt.         "exact_quote": "Let $f:X\\to S$ be an already projective surjective morphism of compact Kähler spaces, with $X$ smooth. Let $(X,B)$ be an effective ordinary real klt pair, and let $D=K_X+B$.         "exact_quote": "Let $f:X\\to Z$ be a projective contraction between normal irreducible compact Kähler spaces. Suppose that $(X,B+\\mathbf M)$ has globally modified-big total boundary and that $$A=[K_X+B+\\mathbf M_X]=f^*\\gamma,\n \\qquad \\gamma\\in H^{1,1}_{\\mathrm{BC}}(Z).$$ There is an adjoint-preserving preparation as in Lemma <a href=\"#prog:base-presentation-preparation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prog:base-presentation-preparation\">44</a>, with multiplier ideal $\\mathcal J_1\\supseteq\\mathcal J_o$, for which $$\\label{prog:base-presentation-Stein}\n R^if_*\\mathcal J_1=0\\quad(i>0),\\qquad\n f_*\\mathcal O_{N_1}=\\mathcal O_Z/(f_*\\mathcal J_1),\n \\qquad N_1=V(\\mathcal J_1).$$ If $N_1$ dominates $Z$, then $f_*\\mathcal J_1=0$. Otherwise there are generalized data $(Z,B_Z+\\mathbf N)$, a projective carrier $\\tau:T\\to Z$ with $T$ smooth and compact Kähler, a real SNC structure divisor $C_T$, and a Kähler class $\\beta_T$ such that $$\\label{prog:base-presentation-identities}\n \\begin{gathered}\n [K_Z+B_Z+\\mathbf N_Z]=\\gamma,\\qquad\n \\tau^*\\gamma=[K_T+C_T]+\\beta_T,\\qquad\n \\mathbf N_T=\\beta_T,\\\\\n B_Z=\\tau_*C_T\\geq0,\\qquad\n B_Z+\\mathbf N_Z\\ \\text{is globally modified big}.\n \\end{gathered}$$ The negative components of $C_T$ are $\\tau$-exceptional, and $$\\label{prog:base-presentation-ideal}\n \\mathcal J_Z:=\\mathcal J(Z,B_Z+\\mathbf N)\n       =\\tau_*\\mathcal O_T(-\\lfloor C_T\\rfloor)\n       \\supseteq f_*\\mathcal J_1.$$ In particular the base data are gklt wherever $f_*\\mathcal J_1$ is the unit ideal. If the source data are gklt, the base data are gklt. All adjoint identities are preserved by pullback to higher models.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prog-base-emc",
        "exact_quote": "Let $D$ be a compact complex space, possibly nonreduced, and let $\\delta\\in H^2(D,\\mathbb R)$ have nonnegative degree on compact curves. Use the definitions of a Moishezon morphism and of a contraction defined by a class in (Hacon and Xie 2026, Definitions 2.32 and 2.34) [[HX](#ref-HX)]. Then the following hold.*\n\n1.  *If $\\delta$ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction, so is its restriction to every closed analytic subspace of $D$.*\n\n2.  *Let $g:D\\to V$ be a projective contraction of compact complex spaces, so $g_*\\mathcal O_D=\\mathcal O_V$, and suppose $\\delta=g^*\\epsilon$ for a class $\\epsilon\\in H^2(V,\\mathbb R)$ having nonnegative degree on compact curves. Then $\\delta$ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction if and only if $\\epsilon$ is endowed with one.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prog-multiplier-transport",
        "exact_quote": "Let $g:X\\to Y$ be a projective bimeromorphic morphism of normal compact Kähler spaces. Suppose effective generalized pair data on $X$ and $Y$ have the same globally nef b-part and are crepant over $Y$. In particular their adjoint classes $A_X$ and $A_Y$ satisfy $A_X=g^*A_Y$ in Bott–Chern cohomology. Write $J_X,J_Y$ for their multiplier ideals and $N_X=V(J_X)$, $N_Y=V(J_Y)$ for their non-klt closed subspaces. Then $$g_*J_X=J_Y,\\qquad R^ig_*J_X=0\\quad(i>0),\n       \\qquad g_*\\mathcal O_{N_X}=\\mathcal O_{N_Y}.$$ The restriction $N_X\\to N_Y$ is a projective contraction. Hence, whenever $A_Y$ is nef, the restriction of $A_X$ to $N_X$ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction if and only if the restriction of $A_Y$ to $N_Y$ is endowed with one.",
        "source_id": "PM-034.1"
      },
      "evidence": [

        "exact_quote": "Use the hypotheses and notation of Proposition <a href=\"#prog:base-presentation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prog:base-presentation\">45</a>. Suppose that $A=f^*\\gamma$ is nef and that its restriction to the original non-klt closed subspace $N_o=V(J_o)$ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction. Put $$I=f_*J_1,\\qquad N_*=V(I)\\subset Z.$$ Then $\\gamma|_{N_*}$ is endowed with a Moishezon contraction. If the prepared non-klt closed subspace $N_1=V(J_1)$ dominates $Z$, then $\\gamma$ and $A$ are endowed with Moishezon contractions. Otherwise the generalized pair supplied on $Z$ has a non-klt closed subspace endowed with the contraction defined by the restricted class of $\\gamma$.         "exact_quote": "Let $f:X\\to Z$ be a projective surjective morphism with connected fibres between normal complex analytic spaces.         "anchor": "stmt-prog-fixed-integral-grid",
        "exact_quote": "Let $X_0$ be a compact Kähler space, and suppose that $$\\alpha_0=\\sum_{j=1}^r a_j\\gamma_{0j},\\qquad a_j>0,\n \\qquad \\gamma_{0j}\\in H^2(X_0,\\mathbb Q),$$ where each $\\gamma_{0j}$ has nonnegative degree on compact curves. Fix integers $m_j>0$ such that $m_j\\gamma_{0j}$ is the image of an integral cohomology class. Consider an existing sequence of projective birational steps $$X_i\\xrightarrow{f_i}Z_i\\xleftarrow{f_i^+}X_{i+1},$$ where $f_i^+$ is the identity for a divisorial step, $f_i$ satisfies Lemma <a href=\"#prog:integral-h2\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prog:integral-h2\">50</a>, and $\\alpha_i$ is trivial on its contracted ray. Assume every $f_i$-contracted curve has degree proportional to that ray for the classes in the display. Then the classes $\\gamma_{ij}$ descend through $f_i$ and pull back through $f_i^+$, the same integers $m_j$ remain integral multiples at every stage, and the transported classes remain nonnegative on curves. In particular, for every integral compact curve $C\\subset X_i$, $$\\alpha_i\\cdot C>0\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n \\alpha_i\\cdot C\\geq\\delta,\n \\qquad \\delta:=\\min_j\\frac{a_j}{m_j}>0.$$",

      },

Consider an existing sequence of projective birational steps $$X_i\\xrightarrow{f_i}Z_i\\xleftarrow{f_i^+}X_{i+1},$$ where $f_i^+$ is the identity for a divisorial step, $f_i$ satisfies Lemma <a href=\"#prog:integral-h2\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prog:integral-h2\">50</a>, and $\\alpha_i$ is trivial on its contracted ray. Assume every $f_i$-contracted curve has degree proportional to that ray for the classes in the display. Then the classes $\\gamma_{ij}$ descend through $f_i$ and pull back through $f_i^+$, the same integers $m_j$ remain integral multiples at every stage, and the transported classes remain nonnegative on curves. In particular, for every integral compact curve $C\\subset X_i$, $$\\alpha_i\\cdot C>0\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n \\alpha_i\\cdot C\\geq\\delta,\n \\qquad \\delta:=\\min_j\\frac{a_j}{m_j}>0.$$",
      "explanation": "Positive rational summands descend with fixed integral multiples and give a uniform gap for positive curve degrees along existing crepant steps.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prog-detected-cohomology",
        "exact_quote": "Let $X_0$ be a smooth compact Kähler manifold. Consider a finite sequence of divisorial contractions and small flips $$X_0\\dashrightarrow X_1\\dashrightarrow\\cdots\n                         \\dashrightarrow X_r$$ between normal globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial compact Kähler spaces with rational singularities. Assume that every negative contraction $f_i:X_i\\to Z_i$ is a projective contraction of one ray of the analytic cone, that $Z_i$ has rational singularities, and that each small flip is the detected flip of a global rational line $L_i$ with $L_i\\cdot R_i<0$. For a divisorial contraction assume the usual single exceptional prime. Then, for every projective smooth resolution $p:U\\to X_i$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n H^2(U,\\mathbb R)\n   &=p^*H^2(X_i,\\mathbb R)\n       \\oplus\\bigoplus_{E\\text{ exceptional for }p}\\mathbb R[E],\\\\\n H^{1,1}(U,\\mathbb R)\n   &=p^*H^{1,1}_{\\rm BC}(X_i,\\mathbb R)\n       \\oplus\\bigoplus_{E\\text{ exceptional for }p}\\mathbb R[E].\n\\end{aligned}$$ The first equality also holds over $\\mathbb Q$. There are compatible forward linear transforms on $H^2(-,\\mathbb R)$ and on Bott–Chern cohomology. They are surjective, are isomorphisms for a small flip, and preserve rational degree-two classes. On a common resolution the pullback difference is an actual exceptional divisor class; for a flip it is exceptional over both spaces.*\n\n*The exceptional quotient also takes the Chern class of a holomorphic line bundle on $U$ to a rational holomorphic line class on $X_i$.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-rank-comparison",
        "exact_quote": "Let $g_0:(X_0,B_0)\\to W_0$ be a fibration with connected fibers from a smooth compact Kähler manifold to a smooth compact manifold in class $\\mathcal C$. Assume $B_0$ is a rational SNC boundary and $\\kappa(F,K_F+B_{0,F})=0$ on very general smooth fibers. After modifications there is a diagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n X \\arrow[r,\"\\pi\"] \\arrow[d,\"g\"'] & X_0 \\arrow[d,\"g_0\"]\\\\\n W \\arrow[r,\"\\rho\"'] & W_0\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ with $X,W$ smooth compact Kähler, $g$ a fibration with connected fibers, and $B=\\pi_*^{-1}B_0+\\operatorname{Exc}(\\pi)_{\\mathrm{red}}$ SNC. Every prime of $X$ whose $g$-image has codimension at least two is $\\pi$-exceptional. There are a rational SNC boundary $T$ on $W$, a surjection $p:W\\to S$ with connected fibers to a smooth projective variety, and a nef rational line $P_S$ on $S$. Put $$M=p^*P_S,\\qquad H=K_W+T+M,\\qquad J=K_X+B.$$ If $\\dim S>0$, then $K_S+a_0P_S$ is big for some rational $a_0>0$; if $S$ is a point, $M\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}0$. There is a rational divisor $A_*$ on $X$ giving an actual rational line identity $$J\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}g^*H+A_*.\n\\label{rank:line-comparison}$$ These data satisfy the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The horizontal part $A_{*,\\mathrm{hor}}$ is effective. On a very general smooth fiber it is the zero divisor of a relative generating section of a divisible multiple of $K_F+B_F$, divided by that multiple.*\n\n\n2.  *For each prime $D\\subset W$, let $E$ run over the primes of $X$ dominating $D$, and put $a_E=\\mathop{\\mathrm{ord}}_E(g^*D)$. Then $$(A_*)_E\\geq0,\\qquad\n           \\min_{E\\to D}\\frac{(A_*)_E}{a_E}=0.\n    \\label{rank:zero-minimum}$$ There is no assertion here about the sign at a prime whose image has codimension at least two.*\n\n\n3.  *For all degrees $q$ divisible by one positive integer, multiplication by the relative generating form identifies $$H^0(W,qH)\\simeq H^0(X,qJ)$$ and preserves ratios of sections. In the same degrees, for every proper holomorphic $h:W\\to V$, there is a natural injection $$(hg)_*\\mathcal O_X(qJ)\\ \\lhook\\joinrel\\longrightarrow\\\n     h_*\\mathcal O_W(qH).\n    \\label{rank:relative-injection}$$*\n\n\n4.  *Let $\\tau:W'\\to W$ be a further smooth modification included in another diagram with the preceding properties over the same reference $X_0$, using the same source-boundary convention. Let $H'$ be the base line produced by that diagram. Then, as actual rational lines, $$H'\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}\\tau^*H+E_H,\n     \\qquad E_H\\geq0\\ \\text{\\(\\tau\\)-exceptional}.\n    \\label{rank:higher-base}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-034.1"
      },

Every prime of $X$ whose $g$-image has codimension at least two is $\\pi$-exceptional. There are a rational SNC boundary $T$ on $W$, a surjection $p:W\\to S$ with connected fibers to a smooth projective variety, and a nef rational line $P_S$ on $S$. Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n R_j&=\\frac{w}{e!}j^e+O(j^{e-1}),\\label{nv:GRR-rank}\\\\\n B_0:=G+\\lim_j\\frac{c_1(\\mathcal F_j)}{jR_j}\n &=\\frac{f_*\\beta^{e+1}}{(e+1)w}\\ge0,\\label{nv:GRR-base}\\\\\n \\int_U\\beta^{b_0+e}\n &\\le (e+1)^{b_0}w\\,\\mathop{\\mathrm{vol}}(B_0).\\label{nv:mixed-bound}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The limit in Equation <a href=\"#nv:GRR-base\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"nv:GRR-base\">[nv:GRR-base]</a> is a limit of real Bott–Chern classes.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $(X,D)$ be a dlt pair on a normal irreducible compact Kähler space, and suppose that the pair has the resolution property of Definition <a href=\"#def:lc-strata-resolution\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:lc-strata-resolution\">16</a>.         "anchor": "stmt-signed-root-charts",
        "exact_quote": "For each $t\\in P$, after shrinking an open neighborhood $U\\subset P$, choose a line $R_U$ together with an isomorphism $R_U^\\ell\\simeq\\mathcal O_P(1)|_U$. A comparison of two such roots on an overlap is power-compatible if its $\\ell$-th power commutes with these isomorphisms. If $t\\notin\\phi(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Supp}}G_+)$, one may take $U$ disjoint from this closed image and set $Z_U=S=T=\\varnothing$; the assertions below are then vacuous for the unique maps from the empty spaces. If $t\\in\\phi(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Supp}}G_+)$, there are a Hausdorff normal analytic space $Z_U$ of pure dimension $n$, considered near a reduced Cartier divisor $S$ of pure dimension $n-1$, a reduced Weil divisor $T$ with no component in common with $S$, and maps $$\\pi:Z_U\\longrightarrow X,\\qquad g:S\\longrightarrow U$$ with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The map $g$ is proper, and $\\pi|_S$ is finite over $D_U=\\phi^{-1}(U)$, with $g=\\phi\\pi|_S$. Its image covers the positive components over $U$, and $$\\mathcal O_S(S)\\simeq g^*R_U.$$ The image of $S\\cap T$ lies in $\\phi(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Supp}}G_+\\cap(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Supp}}G_-\\cup D_0))$. Near $S$, the underlying sets satisfy $$\\pi^{-1}(|D|)=|S|\\cup|T|.$$*\n\n\n2.  *The pair $(Z_U,S+T)$ is log canonical, and there is a fixed actual isomorphism of divisorial sheaves $$\\label{signed:adjoint-chart}\n     \\tau:\\mathcal O_{Z_U}(aS)\\xrightarrow{\\ \\simeq\\ }\\omega_{Z_U}(S+T).$$ The spaces $Z_U$ and $S$ are Cohen–Macaulay. The support of $T$ is locally set-theoretically principal. Off $T$, the space $Z_U$ is klt and its canonical sheaf is invertible. The map $\\pi$ is quasi-finite near $S\\setminus T$.*\n\n3.  *Projective log resolutions of the total divisor data can be chosen with Kähler forms on neighborhoods of the compact sets over each compact fiber of $g$. Power-compatible changes of the boundary root extend to isomorphisms of ambient germs that preserve the full ideal $\\mathcal O_{Z_U}(-S)$, the reduced divisor $T$, and Equation <a href=\"#signed:adjoint-chart\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"signed:adjoint-chart\">[signed:adjoint-chart]</a>.         "anchor": "stmt-signed-localized-hodge",
        "exact_quote": "Let $q:\\mathcal{V}\\to Y$ be a holomorphic map of complex manifolds, submersive near a reduced closed analytic subspace $i:H\\hookrightarrow\\mathcal{V}$ of pure dimension $d$ and codimension $c_0>0$. Suppose $h=q|_H$ is proper. Assume that locally $H$ is an SNC divisor in a smooth submanifold of codimension $c_0-1$, and that a reduced divisor $A$ is simultaneously SNC and transverse to those support equations. Assume that the components $H_i$ and $A_j$ near $H$ have finite global smooth indexing, and that every closed stratum $H_I\\cap A_J$, with $I\\ne\\varnothing$, is smooth and proper over $Y$ and carries a global relative Kähler form. Empty or disconnected strata are allowed. Here $H_I=\\bigcap_{i\\in I}H_i$ and $A_J=\\bigcap_{j\\in J}A_j$, with $A_\\varnothing=\\mathcal{V}$.*\n\n\n\n*Use right $\\mathcal{D}$-modules and finite-pole local cohomology, and put $$\\mathcal K_A=\\mathcal H^{c_0}_{[H]}(\\omega_{\\mathcal{V}})(*A).$$ Its order filtration is generated from $F_0\\mathcal K_A=i_*\\omega_H(A)$, with $F_p=0$ for $p<0$. For $M^j=\\mathcal H^j q_+\\mathcal K_A$, the filtered direct image is strict at every level, and $M^j$ has a finite filtration by submodules, strict for $F$, whose quotients are polarizable real pure Hodge modules. In particular, $$\\label{signed:lowest-step}\n F_0M^j=R^jh_*\\omega_H(A)\\lhook\\joinrel\\longrightarrow M^j,\n \\qquad F_pM^j=0\\quad(p<0).$$ Define the symbol morphism $$\\sigma:F_0M^j\\otimes T_Y\\longrightarrow\\mathop{\\mathrm{gr}}^F_1M^j,\n \\qquad \\sigma(m\\otimes\\xi)=[m\\xi].$$ If $Y$ is smooth projective, then for every ample line $N$ on $Y$, $$\\label{signed:symbol-vanishing}\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathcal O_Y}(N,\\mathop{\\mathrm{ker}}\\sigma)=0.$$ This includes any coherent torsion in the kernel.",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Compact Kähler space** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A compact Kähler space is a compact complex analytic space with a Kähler form in the sense of local strictly plurisubharmonic potentials on local embeddings.
- **Analytic nefness** ([source](#pm-h-3)): For a rational line bundle $L$, analytic nefness means that $c_1(L)$ belongs to the closure of the Kähler cone.
- **Semiample rational line** ([source](#pm-h-3)): We call $L$ semiample if an actual positive integral multiple is a holomorphic line bundle generated by its global sections.
- **Rational holomorphic line equivalence** ([source](#pm-h-7)): Thus $L\sim_{\mathbb Q}L'$ means that $mL$ and $mL'$ are holomorphically isomorphic for some positive integer $m$.
- **Minimal divisorial multiplicity** ([source](#pm-h-7)): For a prime divisor $D$, its minimal multiplicity is $$\nu_D(\alpha)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0} \inf\bigl\{\nu_D(T):T\in\alpha,\ T\geq-\varepsilon\omega\bigr\}.$$
- **Divisorial negative and positive parts** ([source](#pm-h-7)): Boucksom’s divisorial decomposition is $$N(\alpha)=\sum_D\nu_D(\alpha)D, \qquad Z(\alpha)=\alpha-\{N(\alpha)\}.$$
- **Good divisorial decomposition assertion** ([source](#stmt-def-good-decomposition)): For $n\geq0$, let $\mathcal G_n$ be the following assertion. If $X$ is a connected smooth compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $B$ is a rational simple normal crossing boundary with coefficients in $[0,1]$, and $J=K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective, then there is a smooth compact Kähler modification $\mu:Y\to X$ and an actual rational line identity $$\label{bir:good-decomposition} \mu^*J\sim_{\mathbb Q}P+R, \qquad P\text{ semiample},\qquad R=N(\mu^*J)\geq0,$$ where $R$ is a rational divisor.
- **Simple compact space** ([source](#pm-h-9)): A compact space is *simple* if no positive-dimensional proper compact analytic subvariety passes through a very general point.
- **Algebraic dimension notation** ([source](#pm-h-9)): We write $a(X)$ for its algebraic dimension.
- **Global strong factoriality** ([source](#pm-h-11)): It is *globally strongly $\mathbb Q$-factorial* if every global coherent rank-one reflexive sheaf has an invertible reflexive power.
- **Resolution adapted to lc strata** ([source](#stmt-def-lc-strata-resolution)): An effective rational dlt pair $(T,B)$ on a normal compact Kähler space satisfies the *lc-strata resolution convention* if it admits a projective log resolution $r:W\to T$ with smooth compact Kähler source such that the strict boundary and the exceptional support together have distinct smooth components forming a simple normal crossing divisor. Writing $$K_W+B_W^{\mathrm{cr}}=r^*(K_T+B)$$ with compatible canonical choices, every $r$-exceptional coefficient of $B_W^{\mathrm{cr}}$ is strictly less than one, and $r$ is an isomorphism at the general point of every log canonical center of $(T,B)$.
- **Ordinary negative step** ([source](#pm-h-11)): An *ordinary negative step* for $J=K_T+B$ is a projective bimeromorphic divisorial contraction, or a diagram $$T\xrightarrow{f} Z\xleftarrow{f^+}T^+$$ of projective small bimeromorphic morphisms, with connected fibers and normal base, such that $-J$ is $f$-ample and, in the small case, the trace $J^+$ is $f^+$-ample.
- **Globally nef b-class** ([source](#pm-h-11)): A nef b-class is a Bott–Chern class that is globally nef on one fixed smooth compact Kähler carrier, with its linear traces on the other models.
- **Generalized klt** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Generalized klt, abbreviated gklt, means that all generalized log discrepancies, computed on that carrier, are positive.
- **Relative pseudo-effectivity** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Relative pseudo-effectivity means $q_f(\alpha)\in\overline{q_f(\operatorname{Psef}(T))}$, where $\operatorname{Psef}(T)$ is the absolute pseudo-effective cone.
- **Working interval** ([source](#pm-h-13)): The trace $\alpha_i(\lambda)$ is nef on $[\lambda_i,\lambda_{i-1}]$, which we call its *working interval*.
- **Boundary stratum** ([source](#sec:boundary)): A *boundary stratum* is a stratum contained in the reduced floor.
- **Vertical floor** ([source](#floor:semiample-map)): We call $C_Z$ *vertical* if $f_Z(C_Z)\ne Y_Z$; the empty floor is vertical.
- **Comparison arrow** ([source](#floor:class-comparison)): For boundary strata $Z,Z'$ of the same dimension, an *arrow* is a proper bimeromorphic comparison with a projective resolution whose source is smooth and compact Kähler, $$\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] & T\arrow[dl,"p"']\arrow[dr,"p'"]&\\ Z&&Z' \end{tikzcd}$$ such that the two pulled-back adjoint lines are equal as invertible subsheaves of meromorphic $q$-pluricanonical forms on $T$, and $$\label{floor:class-comparison} p^*c_Z-(p')^*c_{Z'}\in\mathop{\mathrm{NS}}(T)_{\mathbb R}.$$
- **Canonical Iitaka base** ([source](#pm-h-40)): We call $Y$ the *canonical Iitaka base*.
- **Compatible invariant generating tuples** ([source](#pm-h-42)): For $d\geq0$ and $k\geq1$, a system of tuples in degree $k$ through dimension $d$ means a vector subspace $$\mathcal V_d(k)\subseteq \bigoplus_{\substack{Z\subset S\text{ a stratum}\\\dim Z\leq d}} H^0(Z,L_Z^k).$$
- **Finite boundary layers** ([source](#pm-h-62)): For every integer $j$ and positive integer $k$, put $$\mathcal A_j=I^j/I^{j+1}=\mathcal O_S(-jS),\qquad \mathcal T_{j,k}=I^j/I^{j+k}.$$

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-negative-part-foundations** [claim](#stmt-bir-calculus) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bir-calculus): Siu decomposition, small Kähler perturbations and generic-order comparison. -> Negative-part calculus and restriction to resolved primes.
- **step-exceptional-and-pullup** [claim](#stmt-bir-exceptional) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bir-exceptional): Mixed Hodge index and exceptional translation, followed by the modified-nef contradiction. -> Exact exceptional translation and pullback of known decompositions.
- **step-fixed-sections-and-transfers** [claim](#stmt-bir-sections) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bir-finite-descent): Fixed vanishing, unique currents, exceptional cancellation and finite analytic norms. -> Descent and resolution stability for actual rational line decompositions.
- **step-projective-anchor** [claim](#stmt-proj-good-models) / [proof](#proof-stmt-proj-good-models): Import the conditional projective good-model theorem and identify its exceptional error analytically. -> Projective good decomposition and projective nef adjoint semiampleness.
- **step-line-descent-and-projectivity** [claim](#stmt-prog-integral-descent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-detected-flip): Consecutive generated powers, degree-zero cohomology descent and a global detector algebra. -> Exact Cartier descent and projective detected contractions and flips.
- **step-relative-klt-and-small-models** [claim](#stmt-prog-relative-klt) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-relative-klt): Fixed local adjoint rings, finite marked models and strict discrepancy increase. -> Finite projective relative klt programs and crepant small strong models.
- **step-polarization-and-relative-cones** [claim](#stmt-prog-actual-line-polarization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-relative-hodge): Fibrewise real ampleness, rational Hodge projection and exceptional line tracing. -> Actual relative polarizations and identification of line-degree rays with analytic rays.
- **step-projective-relative-programs** [claim](#stmt-prog-projective-good-model) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-projective-good-model): Fixed ordinary chart replacements, finite global scaling and rational nef-region descent. -> Chosen projective good models, existing-model semiampleness and specified-scaling Mori output.
- **step-effective-base-data** [claim](#stmt-prog-base-presentation-preparation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-base-presentation): Adjoint-preserving preparation, fibre integration, positive metric extension, regularization and multiplier-ideal comparison. -> Effective generalized base data with a Kähler carrier and controlled multiplier ideals.
- **step-nonklt-contraction-transport** [claim](#stmt-prog-base-emc) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-base-emc-induction): Stein factorization on closed subspaces, crepant multiplier transport and lower-base induction. -> Moishezon contraction conditions descend and restrict with their closed-subspace structures.
- **step-integral-grid-and-cohomology** [claim](#stmt-prog-integral-h2) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-detected-cohomology): Integral exponential and Leray sequences, exact line descent and exceptional direct sums. -> Fixed curve-degree gaps and rational cohomology transport through detected steps and extractions.
- **step-negative-part-base-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prog-negative-part-program) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-nef-good-comparison): Absolute negative-part comparison, vertical divisor descent, perturbed pullback currents and final-error cancellation. -> Semiampleness of the original nef class from a chosen lower-dimensional good model.
- **step-restricted-package-induction** [claim](#stmt-prog-restricted-package) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-restricted-package): Simultaneous dimension induction, with semiampleness before detected steps, chosen relative models before finite geography, and the non-klt contraction assertion last. -> The restricted generalized package and finite positive detected scaling segments.
- **step-ordinary-scalings-and-negative-contraction** [claim](#stmt-prog-nef-trivial) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-contract-negative): Cone-length and Cartier-integrality estimates, finite positive truncations and limiting minimal multiplicities. -> Fixed-nef-line ordinary programs, contraction of precisely the negative primes and lower-dimensional terminal torsion models.
- **step-special-termination** [claim](#stmt-prog-special-termination) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prog-special-termination): Choose a general scaling direction, reduce restricted diagrams to small maps and compare changing slopes with a single affine negative-part interval. -> Eventual floor avoidance and finite nef output for a signed floor-supported adjoint.
- **step-boundary-residue-links** [claim](#stmt-floor-adjunction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-floor-transport): Actual dlt residues, a projective Mori comparison and unimodular unit-stratum transport. -> Unique reduced-union descent and compatible lower restrictions under arrows.
- **step-top-form-and-finite-arrow-actions** [claim](#stmt-floor-top-form-scalar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-floor-torus-scalar-3): Finite Iitaka-base action, symplectic and torus lattice arguments, cyclic roots and bounded selected-resolution cohomology. -> Root-of-unity scalars and finite self-arrow image on vertical strata.
- **step-whole-boundary-generation** [claim](#stmt-floor-generation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-floor-tuples-2): Induction on strata, extension of lower tuples and products over finite isotropy images. -> Generation of an actual Cartier multiple on the whole reduced floor.
- **step-rank-one-preparation** [claim](#stmt-rank-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rank-base-psef): Rank-one relative generators, Hodge line factorization, horizontal negative-part subtraction and extension of descended metric weights. -> A pseudo-effective actual base adjoint and its purely negative form when the base has algebraic dimension zero.
- **step-projective-base-reduction** [claim](#stmt-rank-base-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rank-base-reduction): Relative rational weak Zariski decompositions, a chosen terminating generalized projective program and exact descent of the first nef endpoint through a second program. -> A smaller positive base or an actual nef base line that is big or rationally trivial.
- **step-lift-and-generate** [claim](#stmt-rank-big-nef-generation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rank-big-nef-generation-2): Mixed intersection identification of the full negative divisor, its contraction, boundary generation and exclusion of residual stable base loci. -> Good decomposition in the rank-one and general fibration cases.
- **step-nonvanishing-slopes-and-volumes** [claim](#stmt-nv-meromorphic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-nv-two-slot-volume): Contrary-hypothesis cotangent slope control, very general subvariety classification and a projective bundle with controlled volume. -> A uniform point pole bound and the auxiliary dimensional root scale.
- **step-diagonal-determinant-contradiction** [claim](#stmt-nv-determinant-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-nv-determinant-order-2): Direct-image determinant estimates, diagonal restricted-mass selection, incidence pole transfer and cancellation on a point-blowup slice. -> Meromorphic canonical nonvanishing on simple spaces independently of the projective subadditivity assumption.
- **step-signed-root-and-residue** [claim](#stmt-signed-root-charts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-signed-residue): Numerical boundary separation, compatible root constructions and a split residue comparison retaining residual poles. -> Ordinary signed analytic charts and split cohomological residue insertion.
- **step-all-orders-and-escaping-fibres** [claim](#stmt-signed-all-orders) / [proof](#proof-stmt-signed-escaping-fibers): Localized filtered Hodge direct image, undivided obstruction identities, ample symbol vanishing and analytic approximation of a formal deformation. -> Finite lifting surjectivity on every germ and bounded compact families leaving the boundary.
- **step-signed-rigidity-and-simple-case** [claim](#stmt-signed-torsion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-signed-escaping-fibers-3): Compact cycle-space evaluation and Baire category contradict simplicity; torsion comparison and unique-current subtraction remove the enlarged boundary. -> Purely negative rational decomposition in the simple case.
- **step-global-decomposition-and-abundance** [claim](#stmt-thm-good-decomposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-good-decomposition-2): Dimension induction through algebraic reduction, covering-family evaluation and finite descent, followed by resolution transfer for the nef adjoint. -> Conditional good divisorial decomposition and actual global generation on the original normal space.

          "anchor": "stmt-prog-nef-trivial",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(T,B)$ be an effective rational dlt pair on a globally strongly $\\mathbb Q$-factorial compact Kähler $d$-fold, and put $J=K_T+B$.*\n\n1.  *For a sufficiently large Kähler class $\\omega$, there is an ordinary $J$-program with scaling of $\\omega$, starting with $\\{J\\}+\\omega$ Kähler.           "anchor": "stmt-rank-comparison",
          "exact_quote": "Let $g_0:(X_0,B_0)\\to W_0$ be a fibration with connected fibers from a smooth compact Kähler manifold to a smooth compact manifold in class $\\mathcal C$. Assume $B_0$ is a rational SNC boundary and $\\kappa(F,K_F+B_{0,F})=0$ on very general smooth fibers. After modifications there is a diagram $$\\begin{tikzcd}\n X \\arrow[r,\"\\pi\"] \\arrow[d,\"g\"'] & X_0 \\arrow[d,\"g_0\"]\\\\\n W \\arrow[r,\"\\rho\"'] & W_0\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ with $X,W$ smooth compact Kähler, $g$ a fibration with connected fibers, and $B=\\pi_*^{-1}B_0+\\operatorname{Exc}(\\pi)_{\\mathrm{red}}$ SNC. Every prime of $X$ whose $g$-image has codimension at least two is $\\pi$-exceptional. There are a rational SNC boundary $T$ on $W$, a surjection $p:W\\to S$ with connected fibers to a smooth projective variety, and a nef rational line $P_S$ on $S$. Put $$M=p^*P_S,\\qquad H=K_W+T+M,\\qquad J=K_X+B.$$ If $\\dim S>0$, then $K_S+a_0P_S$ is big for some rational $a_0>0$; if $S$ is a point, $M\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}0$. There is a rational divisor $A_*$ on $X$ giving an actual rational line identity $$J\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}g^*H+A_*.\n\\label{rank:line-comparison}$$ These data satisfy the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The horizontal part $A_{*,\\mathrm{hor}}$ is effective. On a very general smooth fiber it is the zero divisor of a relative generating section of a divisible multiple of $K_F+B_F$, divided by that multiple.*\n\n\n2.  *For each prime $D\\subset W$, let $E$ run over the primes of $X$ dominating $D$, and put $a_E=\\mathop{\\mathrm{ord}}_E(g^*D)$. Then $$(A_*)_E\\geq0,\\qquad\n           \\min_{E\\to D}\\frac{(A_*)_E}{a_E}=0.\n    \\label{rank:zero-minimum}$$ There is no assertion here about the sign at a prime whose image has codimension at least two.*\n\n\n3.  *For all degrees $q$ divisible by one positive integer, multiplication by the relative generating form identifies $$H^0(W,qH)\\simeq H^0(X,qJ)$$ and preserves ratios of sections. In the same degrees, for every proper holomorphic $h:W\\to V$, there is a natural injection $$(hg)_*\\mathcal O_X(qJ)\\ \\lhook\\joinrel\\longrightarrow\\\n     h_*\\mathcal O_W(qH).\n    \\label{rank:relative-injection}$$*\n\n\n4.  *Let $\\tau:W'\\to W$ be a further smooth modification included in another diagram with the preceding properties over the same reference $X_0$, using the same source-boundary convention. Let $H'$ be the base line produced by that diagram. Then, as actual rational lines, $$H'\\sim_{\\mathbb Q}\\tau^*H+E_H,\n     \\qquad E_H\\geq0\\ \\text{\\(\\tau\\)-exceptional}.\n    \\label{rank:higher-base}$$",

          "exact_quote": "Let $X$ be a smooth connected compact Kähler manifold. Suppose that $a(X)=0$ and that no positive-dimensional proper compact analytic subvariety passes through a very general point of $X$. Then $K_X^{\\otimes m}$ has a nonzero meromorphic section for some integer $m>0$.",

          "anchor": "stmt-nv-slope",
          "exact_quote": "Under the contrary hypothesis above, $H^1(X,\\mathcal O_X)=0$, the group $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Pic}}(X)$ is countable, and $L\\ge0$.           "source_id": "PM-034.1"
        },

          "anchor": "stmt-nv-pole-threshold",

If the ordinary analytic Seshadri constant $\\epsilon(K,z')$ is at least $\\eta>0$, then, on the blowup $b:\\widehat W=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Bl}}_zW\\to W$ with exceptional divisor $G$, $$\\label{nv:pole-formula}\n \\sup\\{u\\ge0:b^*\\alpha-u\\{G\\}\\ge0\\}\n \\le \\frac{\\eta}{2}\n     +2^{e-1}\\mathop{\\mathrm{vol}}(\\alpha)\\eta^{-(e-1)} .$$",

          "anchor": "stmt-nv-determinant-order",
          "exact_quote": "On a smooth projective modification $h_+:U^+\\to E^+$ one can choose an approximation $$\\label{nv:plus-decomposition}\n h_+^*(2p_+^*M+s\\zeta)=\\beta^++\\{D^+\\},\n \\qquad \\beta^+\\ \\text{Kähler},\\quad D^+\\ge0\\ \\text{rational},$$ retaining the log-ideal orders of $T|_E$, such that the general fiber volume $w^+$ of $\\beta^+$ over $Z^+$ satisfies $w^+\\ge w/2$. Let $f_+:U^+\\to Z^+$ be the natural map and put $$\\Lambda^+=s h_+^*\\mathcal O_{E^+}(1)-\\mathcal O_{U^+}(D^+),\\qquad\n \\mathcal F_j^+=(f_+)_*\\mathcal O_{U^+}(j\\Lambda^+),\\qquad\n R_j^+=\\mathop{\\mathrm{rk}}\\mathcal F_j^+ .$$ For every sufficiently large divisible $j$, write $$\\iota_j:\\mathcal F_j^+\\hookrightarrow p_+^*\\mathop{\\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\\Omega_Z,\\qquad\n \\varphi_j:\\det\\mathcal F_j^+\\longrightarrow\n       \\bigwedge^{R_j^+}\\!\\bigl(p_+^*\\mathop{\\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\\Omega_Z\\bigr)$$ for the inclusion and its nonzero determinant map. In local frames over $R$, define $$h_j=\\min\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{ord}}_u(c):c\\text{ is a nonzero coefficient of }\\varphi_j\\}.$$ Equivalently, $h_j$ is the minimum order of the maximal minors of $\\iota_j$; it is independent of the frames. If $\\sigma_{J_+}$ is the canonical section of $\\mathcal O_{Z^+}(J_+)$, then $\\varphi_j$ factors as $$\\det\\mathcal F_j^+\n \\xrightarrow{\\ \\cdot\\sigma_{J_+}^{h_j}\\ }\n \\det\\mathcal F_j^+(h_jJ_+)\n \\xrightarrow{\\ \\widetilde\\varphi_j\\ }\n \\bigwedge^{R_j^+}\\!\\bigl(p_+^*\\mathop{\\mathrm{Sym}}^{js}\\Omega_Z\\bigr),$$ where $\\widetilde\\varphi_j$ is holomorphic. The common order satisfies $$\\label{nv:determinant-order-equation}\n h_j\\ge c_n\\,jR_j^+s ,$$ provided $q$ is sufficiently large.",

          "anchor": "stmt-nv-direct-image",
          "exact_quote": "Let $f:U\\to Z_0$ be a surjective projective morphism of smooth connected compact Kähler manifolds, with $\\dim Z_0=b_0\\ge1$ and $\\dim U=b_0+e$, $e\\ge1$.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-signed-root-charts",
          "exact_quote": "For each $t\\in P$, after shrinking an open neighborhood $U\\subset P$, choose a line $R_U$ together with an isomorphism $R_U^\\ell\\simeq\\mathcal O_P(1)|_U$. A comparison of two such roots on an overlap is power-compatible if its $\\ell$-th power commutes with these isomorphisms. If $t\\notin\\phi(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Supp}}G_+)$, one may take $U$ disjoint from this closed image and set $Z_U=S=T=\\varnothing$; the assertions below are then vacuous for the unique maps from the empty spaces. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **conditional-actual-line-abundance**: Under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, analytic nefness of the rational Cartier adjoint of an effective rational log canonical pair on a normal irreducible compact Kähler space implies generation of an actual positive Cartier multiple everywhere.
- **decomposition-retains-holomorphic-line**: The inductive decomposition retains an actual rational holomorphic line identity, a semiample positive part, and the entire analytic divisorial negative part. Equality of Chern classes alone does not supply this conclusion.
- **fixed-integral-grid-through-existing-steps**: Along the specified existing crepant projective steps, the rational summands descend with their original integral multiples and retain nonnegative curve degrees. Positive degrees therefore have the stated uniform positive lower bound.
- **restricted-model-package-scope**: The restricted model package uses globally nef carrier data and globally modified-big total boundary traces. Its birational constructions use detected steps or already projective relative constructions; its general semiample morphisms are asserted to be Moishezon.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **remove-subadditivity-premise**: Treat compact Kähler log abundance as unconditional. -> The main theorem explicitly assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity; omitting that premise changes the asserted result.
- **replace-line-identity-by-class-equality**: Deduce generation of a prescribed holomorphic line solely from an equality of its Chern class with another class. -> The source distinguishes identities of actual rational lines from equality of their Chern classes. The decomposition and descent arguments preserve the former.
- **generate-pseudo-effective-adjoint-directly**: Apply the main generation conclusion directly to an adjoint known only to be pseudo-effective. -> The main theorem requires analytic nefness. The stronger birational theorem instead separates a semiample positive part from an effective fixed negative divisor on a modification.
- **infer-arbitrary-generalized-termination**: Use existence of a chosen relative good model as termination of every generalized flip sequence. -> The restricted relative assertion explicitly concerns a chosen model and excludes such a universal termination assertion.
- **promote-moishezon-map-to-projective**: Treat every semiample contraction produced by the restricted package as projective. -> The source asserts projectivity only where the construction supplies an actual relatively ample line.
- **extend-negative-part-pullback-arbitrarily**: Assume that an arbitrary pseudo-effective class has a negative part commuting with pullback. -> The source expressly avoids this general identity. Its pullback lemmas require a known decomposition with nef positive part.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The main conclusion is an existence theorem for a generated Cartier multiple on arbitrary compact Kähler analytic spaces, conditional on logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity. The source specifies neither a finite computational representation of these spaces nor an effective procedure for finding the multiple. The proof uses analytic limits and a nonconstructive covering argument: “The analytic space $D_i^\circ$ is locally compact and Baire.” The same proof states: “The countable cover just proved contradicts Baire.” These sentences occur at proof-stmt-signed-escaping-fibers-2. Finite tests of an auxiliary intersection or monomial calculation would not decide the geometric existence conclusion at stmt-thm-main.

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


Assume logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity for surjective morphisms with connected fibers between smooth projective complex varieties with compatible reduced simple normal crossing boundaries. We prove log abundance for normal irreducible compact Kähler spaces in every dimension: for a log canonical pair $`(X,\Delta)`$ with effective rational boundary and $`K_X+\Delta`$ ℚ-Cartier, analytic nefness of $`K_X+\Delta`$ implies semiampleness.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

The abundance problem asks when the numerical positivity of a log canonical bundle produces a holomorphic map. More precisely, a nef adjoint should have a positive multiple generated by global sections. On a compact Kähler space, nefness is an analytic condition on a cohomology class, whereas generation is a statement about an actual holomorphic line bundle. The distinction is essential in the nonprojective setting.

We prove log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity for smooth projective varieties with reduced boundary. The argument passes through a stronger birational statement: every pseudo-effective smooth log adjoint has a semiample positive part and an effective rational fixed divisor equal to its analytic divisorial negative part. This form both supports the induction and retains the line-bundle information needed for generation on the original space.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The assumption and the theorem

A compact Kähler space is a compact complex analytic space with a Kähler form in the sense of local strictly plurisubharmonic potentials on local embeddings. For a rational line bundle $L$, analytic nefness means that $c_1(L)$ belongs to the closure of the Kähler cone. Equivalently, fix a Kähler form $\omega$ and an integer $r>0$ for which $rL$ is a line bundle. For every $\varepsilon>0$, that line has a smooth Hermitian metric $h_\varepsilon$ satisfying $$\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{2\pi r}\Theta_{h_\varepsilon}
 \geq-\varepsilon\omega.$$ Smooth metrics and forms on a singular space are understood through local embeddings. We call $L$ semiample if an actual positive integral multiple is a holomorphic line bundle generated by its global sections.

<a id="stmt-asm-log-iitaka"></a>
<div id="asm:log-iitaka" class="assumption">

**Assumption 1** (Logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism with connected fibers between smooth connected projective complex varieties. Let $D_X$ and $D_Y$ be reduced effective simple normal crossing divisors, allowing zero divisors, such that $$\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}(f^*D_Y)\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}(D_X).$$ For a very general smooth fiber $F$, put $D_F=D_X|_F$. Then $$\kappa(X,K_X+D_X)\geq
 \kappa(F,K_F+D_F)+\kappa(Y,K_Y+D_Y).$$ Here $D_F$ is reduced SNC and $K_F+D_F\sim (K_X+D_X)|_F$. The Iitaka dimension is $-\infty$ when all positive integral systems are empty, with $(-\infty)+b=-\infty$ also for $b=-\infty$; the zero divisor on a point has Iitaka dimension zero.

</div>

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces). *Assume Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a>. Let $X$ be a normal irreducible compact Kähler complex analytic space, and let $\Delta\geq0$ be a rational divisor such that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical and $K_X+\Delta$ is rational Cartier. If $K_X+\Delta$ is analytically nef, then it is semiample. Explicitly, there is an integer $m>0$ such that $m(K_X+\Delta)$ is Cartier and $$H^0\bigl(X,\mathcal O_X(m(K_X+\Delta))\bigr)\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_X
 \longrightarrow \mathcal O_X(m(K_X+\Delta))$$ is surjective at every point of $X$.*

</div>

The theorem includes every finite dimension and the zero-boundary case. Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a> is used through the projective good-model theorem stated in Proposition <a href="#proj:good-models" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="proj:good-models">12</a>. The cited proof of that projective theorem uses only its zero-boundary case, on a resolved projective Albanese fibration.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Context and relation to earlier work

In the minimal model program, abundance complements the construction of minimal models: the nef adjoint on a minimal model should determine a canonical fibration. For minimal projective threefolds, Miyaoka proved the case of numerical dimension one and Kawamata completed canonical abundance (Miyaoka 1988; Kawamata 1992) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Miyaoka1988](#ref-Miyaoka1988), [Kawamata1992](#ref-Kawamata1992)]. Keel, Matsuki, and McKernan established log abundance for threefolds (Keel, Matsuki, and McKernan 1994, 2004) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[KMM1994](#ref-KMM1994), [KMM2004](#ref-KMM2004)]. In arbitrary dimension, Birkar, Cascini, Hacon, and McKernan established log terminal models for projective klt pairs with big boundary and pseudo-effective adjoint, and finite generation for big adjoints (Birkar et al. 2010) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[BCHM2010](#ref-BCHM2010)].

The compact Kähler history already points to the importance of simple spaces. Peternell’s threefold theorem isolated the possible case of a simple space not bimeromorphic to a finite quotient of a torus (Peternell 2001) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Peternell2001](#ref-Peternell2001)]; Demailly and Peternell subsequently proved canonical nonvanishing for nef terminal Kähler threefolds, including that case (Demailly and Peternell 2003) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[DemaillyPeternell2003](#ref-DemaillyPeternell2003)]. Höring and Peternell constructed minimal models for normal $\mathbb Q$-factorial terminal compact Kähler threefolds with pseudo-effective canonical class (Höring and Peternell 2016) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[HoeringPeternell2016](#ref-HoeringPeternell2016)]. Campana, Höring, and Peternell treated canonical abundance (F. Campana, Höring, and Peternell 2016, 2023) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[CHP2016](#ref-CHP2016), [CHP2023](#ref-CHP2023)], and Das and Ou established log abundance for compact Kähler log canonical threefolds (Das and Ou 2026, Corollary 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[DasOu2026](#ref-DasOu2026)].

With $D_X=D_Y=0$, Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a> is Iitaka’s classical $C_{n,m}$ inequality $\kappa(X)\geq\kappa(F)+\kappa(Y)$ for algebraic fiber spaces (Cao and Păun 2017, Equation (1.0.1)) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[CaoPaun2017](#ref-CaoPaun2017)]. Cao and Păun proved the analogous logarithmic inequality over an abelian base when the pair on the total space has an effective rational boundary and is klt (Cao and Păun 2017, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[CaoPaun2017](#ref-CaoPaun2017)]. Fujino derives logarithmic subadditivity from the conjectured equality $\kappa_\sigma(X,K_X+D)=\kappa(X,K_X+D)$ for smooth projective $X$ with reduced SNC $D$ (Fujino 2017, 2020) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Fujino2017Subadditivity](#ref-Fujino2017Subadditivity), [Fujino2020Corrigendum](#ref-Fujino2020Corrigendum)]. Hashizume proves the reduced-SNC subadditivity statement when the log canonical divisor of the very general fiber is abundant (Hashizume 2020, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[Hashizume2020](#ref-Hashizume2020)]. Here the implication is used in the other direction: the projective companion (OpenAI 2026c) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[LI](#ref-LI)] derives good models for pseudo-effective projective lc adjoints from Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a>, and those good models anchor the Kähler induction.

Hacon and Xie’s cone theorem, adjunction, relative positivity, and modified-big preparation (Hacon and Xie 2026) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[HX](#ref-HX)] provide analytic inputs for our program constructions. Section <a href="#sec:programs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:programs">3</a> constructs effective generalized base data on a higher carrier, with an exact adjoint pullback identity and a multiplier-ideal inclusion. Fibrewise $L^2$ positivity and regularization give this presentation; its Stein-factor consequence supplies the non-klt induction. The section then proves the restricted semiampleness, proper relative good-model, and finite-model statements needed here, following the dimension-induction strategy of (Hacon and Xie 2026) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[HX](#ref-HX)]. The nef data remain globally nef on a fixed carrier, and the total generalized boundary is globally modified big. Actual rational lines make the selected ray contractions projective; ordinary projective analytic results (Fujino 2022) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[FujinoAnalyticBCHM](#ref-FujinoAnalyticBCHM)] then construct their flips and the relative models. This produces a Kähler pullback description of the relevant Bott–Chern class. Generation of the prescribed holomorphic line requires the additional divisorial decomposition and boundary arguments. The fibration comparison and period positivity come from (OpenAI 2026e) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[CI](#ref-CI)]; the boundary and lifting constructions adapt inputs in (OpenAI 2026b, 2026a) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[CB](#ref-CB), [BL](#ref-BL)]. The precise imported results are stated at their points of use.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### The proof and its main constructions

For a pseudo-effective $(1,1)$-class $\alpha$, $N(\alpha)$ records the least generic vanishing forced along prime divisors. Given a smooth compact Kähler manifold $X$ and a rational SNC boundary $B$ with $J=K_X+B$ pseudo-effective, the induction constructs a modification $\mu:Y\to X$ with $Y$ smooth and $$\mu^*J\sim_{\mathbb Q}P+R,\qquad P\text{ semiample},\qquad
 R=N(c_1(\mu^*J)),$$ as an identity of rational holomorphic line bundles, with $R$ an effective rational divisor. Section <a href="#sec:inductive-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:inductive-reduction">2</a> uses transfer rules, algebraic reduction, and generically finite covers to reduce the induction to projective manifolds, nontrivial fibrations, and simple spaces of algebraic dimension zero. Here simple means that no positive-dimensional proper compact subvariety passes through a very general point.

Section <a href="#sec:programs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:programs">3</a> supplies two program results. For the fibration case it contracts a known negative part while preserving the prescribed nef line. For the simple case it proves special termination for a chosen scaling and reaches a nef model when the pseudo-effective adjoint is rationally equivalent to a divisor supported on the reduced boundary, allowing negative coefficients. The termination argument uses lower-dimensional induction to construct one model on which an interval of perturbed adjoints is nef. On a common resolution their negative multiplicities are affine, whereas every nontrivial wall of the restricted program changes a slope. Hence only finitely many such walls occur.

Section <a href="#sec:boundary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:boundary">4</a> turns generation on separate strata into generation on the entire reduced dlt boundary, adapting Fujino’s method of admissible sections (Fujino 2000, sec. 4) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[Fujino2000](#ref-Fujino2000)]. When a comparison is needed, a Mori contraction realizes Kollár’s residue comparison at the two coefficient-one points of a general $\mathbb P^1$ fiber (Kollár 2012, Definition 13 and Proposition 14) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[Kollar2013Sources](#ref-Kollar2013Sources)]. On a common resolution, the pulled-back restrictions of the ambient Kähler class differ by a real linear combination of Chern classes of line bundles. On a stratum whose boundary dominates the image of the map defined by its semiample adjoint, restriction determines sections. For the remaining strata, we prove finite image for self-comparisons on sufficiently divisible pluricanonical systems using an invariant integral, period and lattice arguments, and a uniform cohomological bound for cyclic covers. Products over these finite images give compatible generating sections, used in both closing arguments.

Section <a href="#sec:rank-one" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:rank-one">5</a> first reduces to fibrations whose very general fiber has log Kodaira dimension zero. On a prepared fibration $g:X\to W$, a relative generating form gives $$K_X+B\sim_{\mathbb Q}g^*H+A_*,\qquad H=K_W+T+M,$$ where $T$ is a rational SNC boundary and $M$ is pulled back from a nef rational line on a projective quotient of $W$. Fiber induction allows us to subtract the part of $A_*$ dominating $W$ from a positive current for $K_X+B$. The resulting metric descends along connected smooth fibers; a zero among the nonnegative coefficients at primes dominating each base prime allows extension, proving $H$ pseudo-effective. If $a(W)=0$, the projective quotient is a point, so $M\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$ and lower-dimensional induction makes $H$ rationally equivalent to its negative divisor. For projective $W$, a reduction via a chosen generalized program derived from Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a> either lowers the positive base dimension, handled by secondary induction, or reaches a nef line that is big or torsion. At a stopping case, an intersection argument identifies the full negative divisor upstairs. A torsion positive part completes the decomposition directly. In the big nef case, Section <a href="#sec:programs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:programs">3</a> contracts that divisor while preserving the nef line; boundary generation, extension, and a new log canonical place at a hypothetical base locus prove semiampleness.

Section <a href="#sec:nonvanishing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:nonvanishing">6</a> proves, independently of Assumption <a href="#asm:log-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="asm:log-iitaka">1</a>, that a positive canonical power has a nonzero meromorphic section on every smooth connected simple compact Kähler manifold of algebraic dimension zero. Ou’s uniruledness and foliation results supply the cotangent slope control (Ou 2025) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[Ou2025](#ref-Ou2025)]. A point-threshold bound for big classes of volume one is contradicted using an auxiliary projective bundle over $X\times X$. The diagonal in its square produces a subsheaf occupying a fixed positive fraction of a symmetric cotangent power of that bundle. A second construction over the diagonal of $X\times X$ forces determinant vanishing which, after restriction to a blowup of $X$, violates the point bound.

Finally, Section <a href="#sec:signed" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:signed">7</a> uses the meromorphic section to obtain, after resolving and enlarging to a reduced SNC boundary, a pseudo-effective adjoint with a signed representative supported there. Section <a href="#sec:programs" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:programs">3</a> gives a nef dlt model, and Section <a href="#sec:boundary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:boundary">4</a> gives generation on its reduced boundary. Pseudo-effectivity of the canonical pullback and an intersection argument isolate positive-dimensional boundary fibers away from components whose signed coefficients are nonpositive. A local root construction adapted from (OpenAI 2026c, Proposition 3.3) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[LI](#ref-LI)] separates the positive and negative divisor supports. An SNC Hodge-module calculation extends the lifting method of (OpenAI 2026a, secs. 10–12) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[BL](#ref-BL)] to residual poles and kills every finite-order obstruction to lifting such a fiber. Douady space and Artin approximation give compact deformations leaving the boundary; compactness of the cycle-space components and relative compactness of bounded-volume cycles allow a Baire argument to produce a covering family. Simplicity forces the actual nef line to be torsion. The program comparison and Lemma <a href="#bir:unique-current" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bir:unique-current">8</a> then permit subtraction of the added boundary, yielding the inductive decomposition.

<a id="sec:inductive-reduction"></a>
### Birational decompositions and the geometric reduction

The proof will produce a semiample line bundle on a smooth model, together with its entire fixed divisorial part. This section makes that statement precise and reduces the induction to two cases: spaces admitting a nontrivial fibration, and simple spaces of algebraic dimension zero.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### The inductive decomposition and its negative part

We use additive notation for rational holomorphic line bundles. Thus $L\sim_{\mathbb Q}L'$ means that $mL$ and $mL'$ are holomorphically isomorphic for some positive integer $m$. If a rational divisor occurs in such an identity, it denotes its associated rational line bundle. In contrast, $c_1(L)$ and $\{D\}=c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))$ denote real Bott–Chern classes. Canonical comparisons are made with the usual local meromorphic canonical identifications. In particular, an identity of lines below contains more information than equality of their Chern classes.

Let $X$ be a smooth compact Kähler manifold and let $\alpha$ be a pseudo-effective real $(1,1)$-class. Fix a Kähler form $\omega$. For a prime divisor $D$, its minimal multiplicity is $$\nu_D(\alpha)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
 \inf\bigl\{\nu_D(T):T\in\alpha,\ T\geq-\varepsilon\omega\bigr\}.$$ Here $T$ ranges over closed currents, and $\nu_D(T)$ is its generic Lelong number; one may equivalently use currents with analytic singularities. The limit is independent of $\omega$. Boucksom’s divisorial decomposition is $$N(\alpha)=\sum_D\nu_D(\alpha)D,
 \qquad Z(\alpha)=\alpha-\{N(\alpha)\}.$$ The sum is a finite effective real divisor, and $Z(\alpha)$ is modified nef: its minimal multiplicity at every prime is zero. We write $N(L)$ and $\nu_D(L)$ for $N(c_1(L))$ and $\nu_D(c_1(L))$. These are the analytic notions, with small Kähler perturbations, throughout the paper. We use the foundational results in (Boucksom 2004, secs. 2–3 and 5) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[Boucksom2004](#ref-Boucksom2004)].

The induction asks for a decomposition that retains both the actual line bundle and this analytic negative divisor.

<a id="stmt-def-good-decomposition"></a>
<div id="def:good-decomposition" class="definition">

**Definition 3**. For $n\geq0$, let $\mathcal G_n$ be the following assertion. If $X$ is a connected smooth compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $B$ is a rational simple normal crossing boundary with coefficients in $[0,1]$, and $J=K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective, then there is a smooth compact Kähler modification $\mu:Y\to X$ and an actual rational line identity <a id="bir:good-decomposition"></a>$$\label{bir:good-decomposition}
 \mu^*J\sim_{\mathbb Q}P+R,
